name: Mucolipidosis II (I-Cell Disease)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Mucolipidosis II

criteria.description: Markedly elevated lysosomal enzymes in plasma due to defective mannose-6-phosphate tagging
Characteristic clinical features including coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, and developmental delay
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GNPTAB gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features plus elevated plasma lysosomal enzymes and/or pathogenic GNPTAB variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires biochemical and/or genetic confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Including thickened skin, prominent forehead, and flat nasal bridge
Including short stature, joint stiffness, and abnormal bone development

common.notes: Including valvular thickening and heart failure

common.symptomName: Coarse granular cytoplasmic inclusions in fibroblasts (I-cells)

laboratory: Normal or decreased lysosomal enzyme activity in cultured fibroblasts
Presence of inclusion bodies (I-cells) in peripheral blood or fibroblasts
imaging: Radiographs showing dysostosis multiplex (e.g., thickened ribs, oar-shaped clavicles, vertebral anomalies)
Cardiac echocardiography demonstrating valvular thickening or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in GNPTAB gene causing deficiency of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase
other: Histopathology showing cytoplasmic inclusion bodies in fibroblasts
Coarse facial features and skeletal abnormalities on clinical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Less severe skeletal involvement in early infancy
Later onset and milder clinical course
Partial deficiency of mannose-6-phosphate tagging enzyme

redFlags: Progressive skeletal deformities with dysostosis multiplex
Markedly elevated plasma lysosomal enzyme levels
references: Neufeld EF, Muenzer J. The mucopolysaccharidoses. In: The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
Cathey SS, et al. GNPTAB mutations cause mucolipidosis II and III alpha/beta. Am J Hum Genet. 2010;86(2): 194-201.
